chapter.title: Threads
chapter.para: Any Rexx thread may use any PyObject, and any Python thread any interpreter and any oorexx.RexxObject. Rexx threads (START, REPLY) and Python threads (threading, a thread pool) can call each other at once, in both directions, with callbacks.

Two global locks meet: Python's GIL, which a thread must hold to run Python code, and ooRexx's kernel lock, which a thread must hold to run Rexx code. The bridge never holds one while it waits for the other: a call to Python releases ooRexx's kernel lock, so other Rexx threads run while Python works, and a call to Rexx releases the GIL, so other Python threads run while Rexx works.
A Python thread that uses an interpreter attaches to it for the call, and detaches after. The methods of PyObject are unguarded, so a proxy is never locked by a thread that is in Python.

example.title: A Python thread pool calling a Rexx routine
example.programlisting:
import concurrent.futures, oorexx
with oorexx.Interpreter() as rexx: square = rexx.routine("return arg(1) ** 2") with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as pool: print(sum(pool.map(square, range(100))))

section.title: ADDRESS Environments and Threads
section.para: ADDRESS environments can be registered at any time, from any thread, also while other threads run Rexx in the same interpreter, and several threads may send commands to the same environment at once: a runs each command on the thread that issued it. (Before ooRexx 5.3.0 r13275 registering could crash it: ooRexx bugs #2111 and #2112.)
